experiment: Xyce against VACASK on fast edges and on a bistable nodeset (e2e 15 and 18, phase 2): e2e 15's dmStepResponse (vamos's render of deck_noxf.scs -E, the differential pulse with transres edges, 1e-9 x stop = 2 fs, under GEAR and TRAP, and with 1 ns edges) on Xyce, the 2 fs edges on VACASK (the render trimmed to the tran); a vcvs Schmitt trigger at vin = 0 (gain 10, diode-limited output, vamos-authored: the row's own deck was not kept) with nodeset out=1.7 on VACASK, .NODESET V(OUT)=1.7, with V(P) and with V(X) on Xyce, and at gain 1000 on VACASK
result: the bench's transient fails on Xyce with "Time step too small near step number: 15" (the row: 14 or 15), exit 1 and a header-only print file, under TRAP and GEAR when its pulse edges are 2 fs, and runs with 1 ns edges; VACASK takes the 2 fs edges; away from the edges the two agree within 3e-4 (0.2, 0.5 and 1.5 us); on the Schmitt trigger VACASK's nodeset={"out",1.7} gives the high state (1.7486 V here, 1.70127 V on the row's deck), while Xyce's .NODESET V(OUT)=1.7 converges to the metastable 0 V (adding V(P) changes nothing, and V(X) on the vcvs output gives "Numerically singular matrix found by Amesos"); at gain 1000 VACASK lands on 0 V too
rules: §3.8.1 / §4.5: a pulse without rise and fall gets transres's edge (1e-9 x stop) on both engines, which stops Xyce's transient of a fast bench; e2e 15 writes its edges
§5.5 / §14: a nodeset is a hint the engines may honour differently; e2e 18 checks the nodeset on a circuit with one state only
